job.title: Sales Representative
job.description:
Sales Representative – Paid Training + Uncapped Commission


No cold calling. No prospecting for appointments. Prospects are provided.


A leading hospitality and vacation ownership organization in Las Vegas is expanding its sales team and seeking confident, motivated professionals who want to build a high-income sales career.


No timeshare experience required.


If you have experience in automotive sales, solar sales, real estate, telecommunications, door-to-door sales, retail, hospitality, customer service, or another customer-facing environment, your skills may transfer well to this opportunity.


Why This Sales Opportunity Stands Out

  • No cold calling or prospecting for appointments
  • Pre-qualified prospective customers are provided to you
  • Paid, in-depth sales training
  • Ongoing coaching and development
  • Uncapped commission earning potential
  • Commission opportunities up to 11%
  • Typical first-year earning potential of approximately $60,000–$90,000
  • Opportunity to earn significantly more based on individual performance


What You'll Do

As a Sales Representative, you'll meet face-to-face with prospective customers and current guests, learn about their vacation interests, and introduce them to vacation ownership opportunities.

  • Conduct scheduled vacation ownership presentations with qualified prospective customers
  • Build rapport, ask questions, and identify customer needs
  • Present ownership options, features, and benefits
  • Answer questions and help customers make informed purchasing decisions
  • Complete required sales paperwork and documentation
  • Follow established sales and transaction procedures
  • Participate in sales meetings, training, and ongoing coaching

Continually develop your presentation and closing skills


Who We're Looking For

Previous timeshare experience is not required. We're looking for people who are confident with customers, motivated by results, coachable, dependable, and comfortable in a performance-driven sales environment.

  • Sales experience in automotive, solar, real estate, telecommunications, door-to-door, retail, or another sales environment; OR strong hospitality/customer service experience and a desire to move into sales
  • Strong verbal communication and presentation skills
  • Persuasive, personable, and comfortable speaking face-to-face with customers
  • Motivated by commission and uncapped earning potential
  • Coachable and willing to learn a structured sales process
  • Dependable, adaptable, and comfortable in a fast-paced environment
  • Reliable transportation
  • Ability to work onsite in Las Vegas


Licensing

You do not need to currently hold a timeshare license to apply.

A Nevada timeshare or qualifying real estate license is required before you can begin selling. Candidates who are not currently licensed will need to complete the Nevada timeshare licensing process before beginning sales training.


Compensation

This is a 1099 independent-contractor, commission-based sales opportunity with a draw against earned commissions.

  • Typical first-year earning potential: approximately $60,000–$90,000
  • Commission opportunities up to 11%
  • Uncapped earning potential
  • Higher earnings are possible based on individual sales performance
  • Paid sales training
  • Additional travel-related membership benefits and discounts are available


Ready to Build a Career in Sales?

If you're confident with people, motivated by results, and interested in an opportunity where customers are provided and your earning potential isn't capped, we want to hear from you.

job.title: Production Supervisor
job.description:
Manufacturing Production Supervisor

Job Summary

A leading North American manufacturer of exterior building products is seeking a Manufacturing Production Supervisor to oversee daily plant operations and lead production employees in achieving safety, quality, efficiency, and on-time delivery goals.

This is an excellent opportunity for an emerging manufacturing leader to develop operational expertise and prepare for future leadership opportunities within a growing, established manufacturing organization.

Key Responsibilities

  • Supervise, coach, and develop production team members to achieve performance goals.
  • Coordinate daily production schedules, staffing, workflow, and shift activities.
  • Monitor key performance indicators, including productivity, scrap, downtime, labor efficiency, and equipment effectiveness.
  • Ensure compliance with safety regulations, quality standards, and established operating procedures.
  • Investigate production issues, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean Manufacturing, 5S, and other process improvement methodologies.
  • Partner with maintenance, engineering, quality, and supply chain teams to improve production performance.
  • Monitor material flow, equipment utilization, and changeover efficiency.
  • Maintain accurate production records and shift reports.
  • Foster a collaborative, safety-focused work environment.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Industrial Technology, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 2 years of manufacturing experience, including internships.
  • Knowledge of manufacturing processes, production metrics, and workflow optimization.
  • Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Working knowledge of OSHA requirements and quality standards.
  • Proficiency with ERP/MRP systems and Microsoft Office.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in high-volume or continuous-flow manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, or continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Experience tracking OEE, SPC, or other production performance metrics.
  • Demonstrated ability to coach employees, develop teams, and lead change.
  • Mechanical aptitude and familiarity with industrial equipment.
  • Experience in a made-to-order manufacturing environment is a plus.

Work Environment

This role operates in a manufacturing plant with exposure to machinery, noise, and varying temperatures. The position requires the ability to stand, walk, bend, and lift approximately 25–40 pounds as needed. Occasional overtime or shift flexibility may be required.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with company matching
  • Paid time off and holiday pay
  • Employee discount programs
  • Career advancement and leadership development opportunities

About the Company

Our client is an established North American manufacturer of exterior building products serving residential, light commercial, and multifamily markets. With decades of industry experience, multiple manufacturing facilities, and a strong commitment to innovation, safety, and customer satisfaction, the organization offers employees the opportunity to contribute to a long-standing business while developing their careers.

If you are a motivated manufacturing professional ready to take the next step in your leadership career, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Driver Recruiter Support Specialist/CSR
job.description:
CDL Driver Recruiting Support Specialist

Stevens Transport | Dallas, TX


About Stevens Transport

Stevens Transport is North America’s premier refrigerated transportation company, providing transportation and logistics solutions throughout the United States, Canada, and Mexico. With over 40 years of industry experience, we are proud of our financial stability, commitment to our employees, and family-oriented culture.


Why Join Stevens Transport?

At Stevens, our people are our greatest asset. We offer competitive compensation, benefits, and opportunities for career growth within an established, debt-free transportation and logistics organization.

Compensation: 19.00 per hour + Bonus Structure


Position Summary

Stevens Transport is seeking a motivated, detail-oriented CDL Driver Recruiting Support Specialist to connect with prospective truck drivers, screen applicants, and support the driver recruiting team. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working with people, making calls, and helping candidates navigate the initial stages of the recruiting process.


Key Responsibilities

  • Contact prospective CDL drivers through warm leads, outbound calls, email, and referrals.
  • Explain driving opportunities and generate interest in joining Stevens Transport.
  • Screen applicants to determine qualifications and eligibility.
  • Review applications, driving records, employment history, and required documentation.
  • Maintain accurate candidate records and update applicant tracking systems.
  • Schedule and confirm interviews with Driver Recruiters.
  • Communicate with candidates throughout the early recruiting process.
  • Partner with recruiters to identify qualified candidates and support hiring goals.
  • Prepare recruiting reports and ensure compliance with applicable DOT/FMCSA regulations and company policies.


Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Strong communication, customer service, and telephone skills.
  • Comfortable handling a high volume of inbound and outbound calls.
  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel.
  • Excellent organization, attention to detail, and follow-through.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience with applicant tracking systems (ATS) preferred.
  • Previous recruiting, sales, customer service, or transportation industry experience is a plus.
  • Experience with Tenstreet ATS and knowledge of CDL/FMCSA requirements are preferred.


Join Our Team

If you enjoy connecting with people, identifying qualified candidates, and contributing to a successful recruiting team, Stevens Transport offers an opportunity to build a rewarding career with an established industry leader.

job.title: Border Patrol Agent (BPA) - EVERGREEN
job.description:
U.S. BORDER PATROL AGENT (BPA) | GL-5, GL-7, GL-9 AND GS-11

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is recruiting for full-time Border Patrol Agent career opportunities. Candidates with qualifying general experience, education, public safety, security, military police, or law enforcement experience may be eligible for consideration at different grade levels.


GRADE LEVELS GL-5 AND GL-7

Duties

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is calling on those who want to help protect American interests and secure our Nation. DHS Components work collectively to prevent terrorism; secure borders and our transportation systems; protect the President and other dignitaries; enforce and administer immigration laws; safeguard cyberspace; and ensure resilience to disasters. We achieve these vital missions through a workforce spanning hundreds of occupations. Make an impact; join DHS.


Being a Border Patrol Agent makes you a valuable member of the Federal Law Enforcement Officer (LEO) profession. Typical assignments include:

  • Detecting and questioning persons suspected of violating immigration and custom laws and inspecting documents and possessions to determine citizenship or violations
  • Preventing, and apprehending undocumented noncitizens and smugglers of noncitizens at or near the borders by maintaining surveillance from covert positions to include using infrared scopes during night operations
  • Interpreting and following tracks, marks, and other physical evidence of illegal entry of persons or contraband
  • Performing farm checks, building checks, traffic checks, city patrols, and transportation checks
  • Patrolling the international boundary and coastal waterways using a variety of Government assets such as vehicles, horses, vessels, watercrafts, off-road vehicles, ATVs, snowmobiles, and motorcycles for the accomplishment of the USBP Mission.


Salary and Benefits: Selections may be at the GL-5, GL-7, GL-9, or GS-11 grade levels, with promotion potential to GS-12. Annual base salary for newly appointed Border Patrol Agents ranges from $51,632 to $124,717, depending on grade and applicable pay. Promotions are not guaranteed and are at the discretion of CBP. Base pay does not include potential overtime, recruitment or retention incentives, or future pay adjustments. Federal employment benefits include health and dental benefits, leave, and retirement benefits.

Retention Incentive: Newly appointed Border Patrol Agents may also qualify for up to $30,000 in additional incentives distributed over three years.

Recruitment Incentive: Newly appointed Border Patrol Agents may be offered up to $20,000. The first $10,000 is paid upon successful completion of the academy; an additional $10,000 is available for qualifying prioritized locations.


Current Federal Employees: Offers will only be made at the GL-5 or GL-7 grade levels. Applying to this GL-5/7 announcement may require you to take a change to lower grade which will reduce your salary based on Federal pay regulations. Grade level re-promotions are at the discretion of the U.S. Border Patrol.


Duty Locations: You will be asked to select your preferred location for one of the following mission critical locations:

·  Big Bend Sector Stations - Alpine, Marfa, Presidio, *Sanderson, *Sierra Blanca

·  Blaine Sector Stations - Blaine, Bellingham, Port Angeles, Sumas

·  Buffalo Sector Stations - Oswego

·  Del Rio Sector Stations - *Comstock

·  El Paso Sector Stations - Deming, *Lordsburg

·  Grand Forks Sector Stations - Bottineau, International Falls, Pembina, Portal, Warroad

·  Havre Sector Stations - Malta, Plentywood, Scobey, Sweetgrass

·  Houlton Sector Stations - Calais, Houlton, Rangeley, Van Buren

·  Laredo Sector Stations - Laredo West, *Hebbronville, *Freer

·  New Orleans Sector Stations - Baton Rouge, Lake Charles, New Orleans

·  San Diego Sector Stations - Boulevard, Brownfield, Campo

·  Swanton Sector Stations - Beecher Falls, Massena, Newport, Ogdensburg, Richford, Swanton

·  Tucson Sector Stations - Douglas, Brian A Terry, Three Points Substation

·  Yuma Sector Stations - Blythe, *Ajo


NOTE: The above preference locations are expected to have vacancies available in the future, however, if the duty locations do not have vacancies at the time of your final offer, you may be offered a duty location in another geographic location within the United States.


*Additional $10K Recruitment Incentive: Newly appointed Border Patrol Agents who select a prioritized location will receive an additional $10,000 incentive (total of $20,000). Prioritized locations include Sierra Blanca, TX; Presidio, TX; Sanderson, TX; Comstock, TX; Lordsburg, NM; Freer, TX; Hebbronville, TX; Ajo, AZ.


Bargaining Unit: This position is covered under the National Border Patrol Council (NBPC).


Firearm Proficiency: This position requires you to carry a firearm. Firearm proficiency is required for all Border Patrol Agents and is part of the training provided.


Requirements


Conditions of employment

All pre-employment processes will be conducted in English.

 

Polygraph Examination: You will be required to undergo a polygraph exam and must have favorable results in order to continue in the process. For more information, see Polygraph Examination. NOTE: CBP may accept the results of a prior federal polygraph exam in lieu of a CBP polygraph exam. Certain veterans may be eligible for a polygraph waiver.



Formal Training: You will be detailed to the U.S. Border Patrol Academy in Artesia, New Mexico, for approximately 6 months of intensive instruction in immigration and nationality laws, Border Patrol-specific operations and other courses. Successful completion of the academy is required for this position.


Age Requirement: In accordance with Public Law 100-238, this position is covered under law enforcement retirement provisions. Candidates must be referred for selection to this position before their 40th birthday in accordance with DHS Directive 251-03. The age restriction may not apply if you are currently serving or have previously served in a federal civilian law enforcement (non-military) position covered by Title 5 U.S.C. 8336(c) or Title 5 U.S.C. 8412(d). The age restriction does not apply if you are a Veterans' Preference eligible.


Firearm Requirement: This position requires that the incumbent meet initial and continuing qualifications in the use of firearms as outlined in the Gun Control Act of 1968, amended by the Lautenberg Amendment of 1996. An applicant whose background includes any of the following will be ineligible for consideration: 1) convicted of a crime punishable by imprisonment exceeding one year; 2) has any outstanding warrants or is a fugitive from justice; 3) unlawful user of or addicted to any controlled substance; 4) adjudicated as a mental defective or has been committed to a mental institution; 5) illegally or unlawfully in the United States; 6) renounced U. S. citizenship; 7) subject to a court-ordered restraining (protection) order from harassing, stalking, or threatening an intimate partner (spouse, former spouse, parent of applicant's child, individual who cohabitates or has cohabitated with the applicant), or child; or 8) convicted under Federal, State, or Tribal Court of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence against an intimate partner or child.


More requirements listed below.


Qualifications

Qualifications must be met by the closing date of this announcement.


You qualify for the GL-5 grade level if you possess one of the following:


Experience: One year of general experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level that demonstrates the ability to take charge, make sound decisions, and maintain composure in stressful situations; to learn regulations, methods, and techniques through classroom training and/or on-the-job instruction; and the ability to gather concise information through questioning, observation, and examination of documents and records; OR


Education Substitution: A conferred bachelor's degree or successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in any field leading to a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university; OR


Combination of Experience and Education: A combination of general experience AND successfully completed college education. This will be calculated using your resume and official or unofficial transcripts submitted with your application.



You qualify for the GL-7 grade level if you possess one of the following:


Experience: One year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level that shows you have the experience in law enforcement or other responsible work that demonstrates the skills necessary to:

  • Make sound judgments and decisions in the use of firearms.
  • Deal effectively with people in a courteous and tactful manner in connection with law enforcement matters.
  • Analyze information rapidly and make prompt decisions where you will be expected to make arrests after the completion of required training and apply these skills in a law enforcement capacity such as criminal code enforcement, determining violations of laws, correctional or rehabilitation work involving criminal offenders, security, military, etc.

The above experience will be applied in connection with the Border Patrol Individual Occupational Requirement: Make arrests and exercise sound judgment in the use of firearms; deal effectively with people in a courteous manner in connection with law enforcement matters; analyze information rapidly and make prompt decisions; or develop and maintain contact with a network of informants.


Education Substitution: A conferred bachelor's degree with superior academic achievement, which is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average (i.e., GPA of 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0), or (3) honor society membership. Submitted transcripts must show the applicant does not have more than 10% pass/fail courses in order to qualify for SAA with GPA; OR


One full year of graduate level education in a field of study related to law enforcement (e.g., criminal justice, homeland security, justice studies, law enforcement, courts and judicial systems, forensic technology, forensic psychology, corrections and rehabilitation) or one year of law school from an accredited college or university; OR


Combination of Experience and Education: A combination of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level AND graduate level education completed in a field of study related to law enforcement from an accredited college or university. This will be calculated using your resume and official or unofficial transcripts submitted with your application.


If you have previous or current law enforcement or military law enforcement experience, you may qualify at the GL-9 or GS-11 grade level. See the qualifications below.


National Service Experience: refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.


Experience as a CBP Explorer may be qualifying if your resume provides sufficient information to credit your experience. To receive full credit for your experience, please be sure to describe your duties, roles and responsibilities in detail.


Background Investigation: This position is a sensitive National Security position and, upon selection, applicants will be required to undergo, and must successfully pass, a Tier 5 investigation or equivalent for placement and retention.


Language Proficiency: Border Patrol work requires the ability to speak and read Spanish, as well as English. Agents will be provided training to become proficient with the Spanish language at the academy.


Uniform/Grooming Standards: This position requires wearing an officially approved uniform and complying with established grooming standards; as established by the Border Patrol's Uniform and Grooming Standards Policy #IOP-5320-02A-UGSBPA. Updated guidance: Please note that in accordance with these standards, tattoos and/or brandings on the head or face are not permitted. Obscene, derogatory and/or gang tattoos or brandings shall not be visible.

Education

See the Qualifications Section for education substitution.


Entrance Exam: As part of the pre-employment process, you must complete and pass the Border Patrol Agent Entrance Exam


Medical Requirements: Following a tentative job offer, candidates must undergo and successfully complete a medical screening process. Individuals must be medically and physically capable of performing the essential job functions and duties of the position safely and efficiently without endangering the health and safety of the individual, others, or national security.


Drug Testing Requirements: Employees are subject to drug testing in compliance with the DHS Drug-Free Workplace Program. You must complete a drug test as a condition of employment.


Physical Fitness Test: You will be required to successfully pass the Fitness Test.


Interview Process: You will be required to pass a structured interview.


Rigorous Law Enforcement Officer Special Retirement Coverage: This is a rigorous position subject to mandatory retirement under the special retirement provisions for law enforcement officers under CSRS and FERS (5 CFR 842.803 and 5 CFR 831.903, Conditions for Coverage; 5 USC 8425(b) and 5 USC 8335(b), Mandatory Separation; and 5 USC 8412(d) and 5 USC 8336(c), Immediate Retirement). For more information on required years of service and retirement age, click on this link. For further information on when an employee continues or discontinues coverage under the special retirement system for law enforcement officers, please see the CSRS and FERS handbook, Chapter 46 (CSRS pages 12-14, and FERS pages 41-43). If you have questions regarding your retirement coverage provisions, please contact the CBP Retirement Operations Center at (202) 863-6180.



Additional information

You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this position.


Probationary Period: You must serve a one-year probationary period during the first year of your initial permanent federal appointment.


Driver's License: You must possess the ability to operate a Government Owned Vehicle. A valid driver's license is required. Any legal restrictions on a driver's license are not acceptable.


Misdemeanor Crime of Domestic Violence: The BPA position is a weapons-carrying position. Any person who has been convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence cannot lawfully possess a firearm or ammunition. Therefore, if you have been convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence, you are not qualified for this position.


After you successfully complete all required pre-employment steps, CBP will determine eligibility for a final offer.


Residency Requirement: U.S. Customs and Border Protection has a residency requirement that applies to all applicants not currently employed by CBP. Individuals are required to have physically resided in the United States or its protectorates (as declared under international law) for at least three (3) of the last five (5) years, before completing an application for CBP employment. If you do not meet the residency requirement and you have been physically located in a foreign location for more than two (2) of the last five (5) years, you may request an exception to determine if you are eligible for a residency waiver by meeting one or more of the following conditions:

1. Working for the U.S. Government as a federal civilian or as a member of the military

2. A dependent of a federal civilian or member of the military who was working for the U.S. Government

3. Working as a contractor employee, a volunteer, consultant or an intern for the U.S. Government

4. Participation in a study abroad program sponsored by a U.S. affiliated college or university

If selected for a position, you must provide documentation to support a request for an exception to the residency requirement.


Career Transition Assistance Program (CTAP) and Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP): To be considered, you must submit the documentation listed in the Required Documents section. View information about CTAP/ICTAP eligibility on OPM's Career Transition Resources website.


The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is committed to ensuring that all of our employees act in a manner that embodies the Department's Mission Statement: With honor and integrity, we will safeguard the American people, our homeland and our values. As an employee of CBP, you will be joining a workforce that is dedicated to accomplishing our mission while maintaining the trust of our Nation by strictly adhering to all government ethics standards. Your conduct will be subject to the ethics rules applicable to all Executive Branch employees, and to CBP employees specifically, as well as the criminal conflict of interest statutes. Once you enter on duty, these rules include obtaining approval for outside employment or business activity, to ensure such employment or business activity is not prohibited and does not interfere or conflict with performance of your official duties


Expand additional information

Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution.


Benefits

How you will be evaluated

You will be evaluated for this job based on how well you meet the qualifications above.

This is a Direct Hire Authority announcement. All applicants who meet the minimum qualification requirements will be reviewed. Veteran's Preference and traditional rating and ranking of applicants do not apply to this vacancy. Veterans and Military Spouses will be considered along with all other candidates.


Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., resume, supporting documents, etc.). Review the Qualifications section of this announcement for more information. If you are found qualified and receive a tentative job offer, you will be required to complete and pass all required pre-employment steps before you can receive a final offer.


Note: The following document requirements relate to a potential subsequent federal employment application, not to CBP Talent Network registration.

Required Documents

All applicants are required to submit a resume.


Resume: A resume in English is required. It must contain your full legal name, phone number, complete work history, a detailed description of your duties, the dates you performed those duties (MM/DD/YY), as well as your hours worked per week. If you are a current or former Federal employee you must include your grade and step information to receive credit for that work experience.

Note: Your resume must only be two pages or less and uploaded under the document type - Resume. No additional document types will be reviewed as part of your resume. Please see the Border Patrol Agent Resume Aid for specific information and examples.



Are you qualifying based on education? Submit a copy of your college transcript (an unofficial transcript is acceptable at this time) from an accredited institution. An official transcript will be required prior to entrance on duty. Transcripts must be in English. Education must be from an institution accredited by an agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. Education obtained from a foreign university or college is not creditable unless it has been evaluated by an organization that specializes in interpretation of education credentials; see www.naces.org for a listing of some accrediting agencies. If submitting documentation of a foreign evaluation, a transcript is also required. For more information, see Recognition of Foreign Qualifications.


Are you a current or former federal employee? If you are a current/former federal employee, it is recommended you submit your most recent SF-50 "Notification of Personnel Action" form to support your experience. Please do not submit a Performance Award SF-50.


Are you a veteran? If you claim veterans' preference you will be required to submit proof of eligibility as appropriate to your preference type. For more information, see Veterans Preference.

  • 5-point Preference (TP): Submit DD-214 listing the character of service and either qualifying medal(s) or service period.
  • 10-point Preference (CP or CPS): Submit DD-214 listing the character of service and a VA Disability Award letter dated 1991 or later showing the total percentage of the service-connected disability. Submitting an SF-15 with your application is encouraged.
  • 10-point Preference (XP): You MUST submit a Standard Form 15, DD-214 listing the character of service, and the required documentation stated on the SF-15.
  • Currently Serving: If you are currently serving on active duty, or in the National Guard or Reserves, you can submit a written signed statement from the Armed Forces certifying your dates of service, rank, campaign badge(s) and expeditionary medal(s) (if applicable), expected character of service, type of discharge and anticipated date of separation which must be within 120 days from the closing date of this announcement. Prior to entering on duty, you will be required to provide a final DD-214. Members of the Guard and Reserve can submit the most current copy of their Retirement Points Account System (RPAS) document.


Can you claim an age waiver based on Veterans' Preference or previous Law Enforcement service? If you are over the age of 40, you will need to submit proof you are eligible for an age waiver based on either previous federal law enforcement service or veterans' preference. If you are over the maximum age and do not provide the required documentation for an age waiver, you will not receive consideration under this announcement.

  • If you are claiming an age waiver based on Federal law enforcement service, you MUST submit copies of your SF-50s reflecting the beginning date and end date for all creditable Federal civilian (not military) service under Title 5 U.S.C. 8331(20), and Title 5 U.S.C. 8401(17) showing Retirement Code M or O in Block 30 of your SF-50s.
  • If you are claiming an age waiver based on Veterans' Preference, you must submit the required Veterans' Preference documents.


Are you claiming special priority selection rights under the Career Transition Assistance Program (CTAP) or Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP)? You must submit the separation notice from your agency, your most recent performance rating and your most recent SF-50 with your current position, grade level, and duty location.


If you are relying on your education to meet qualification requirements:

Education must be accredited by an accrediting institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education in order for it to be credited towards qualifications. Therefore, provide only the attendance and/or degrees from schools accredited by accrediting institutions recognized by the U.S. Department of Education.

Failure to provide all of the required information as stated in this vacancy announcement may result in an ineligible rating or may affect the overall rating.

NOTE: The above preference locations are expected to have vacancies available in the future, however, if the duty locations do not have vacancies at the time of your final offer, you may be offered a duty location in another geographic location within the United States.

Prioritized locations include Sierra Blanca, TX; Presidio, TX; Sanderson, TX; Comstock, TX; Lordsburg, NM; Freer, TX; Hebbronville, TX; Ajo, AZ.


Bargaining Unit: This position is covered under the National Border Patrol Council (NBPC).


Firearm Proficiency: This position requires you to carry a firearm. Firearm proficiency is required for all Border Patrol Agents and is part of the training provided.


Requirements

Conditions of employment

All pre-employment processes will be conducted in English.

 

Polygraph Examination: You will be required to undergo a polygraph exam and must have favorable results in order to continue in the process. NOTE: CBP may accept the results of a prior federal polygraph exam in lieu of a CBP polygraph exam. Certain veterans may be eligible for a polygraph waiver.


Formal Training: You will be detailed to the U.S. Border Patrol Academy in Artesia, New Mexico, for approximately 6 months of intensive instruction in immigration and nationality laws, Border Patrol-specific operations and other courses. Successful completion of the academy is required for this position. For more information, please see the Hiring Process Deep Dive Video: Preparing for the Border Patrol Academy


Age Requirement: In accordance with Public Law 100-238, this position is covered under law enforcement retirement provisions. Candidates must be referred for selection to this position before their 40th birthday in accordance with DHS Directive 251-03. The age restriction may not apply if you are currently serving or have previously served in a federal civilian law enforcement (non-military) position covered by Title 5 U.S.C. 8336(c) or Title 5 U.S.C. 8412(d). The age restriction does not apply if you are a Veterans' Preference eligible.


Firearm Requirement: This position requires that the incumbent meet initial and continuing qualifications in the use of firearms as outlined in the Gun Control Act of 1968, amended by the Lautenberg Amendment of 1996. An applicant whose background includes any of the following will be ineligible for consideration: 1) convicted of a crime punishable by imprisonment exceeding one year; 2) has any outstanding warrants or is a fugitive from justice; 3) unlawful user of or addicted to any controlled substance; 4) adjudicated as a mental defective or has been committed to a mental institution; 5) illegally or unlawfully in the United States; 6) renounced U. S. citizenship; 7) subject to a court-ordered restraining (protection) order from harassing, stalking, or threatening an intimate partner (spouse, former spouse, parent of applicant's child, individual who cohabitates or has cohabitated with the applicant), or child; or 8) convicted under Federal, State, or Tribal Court of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence against an intimate partner or child.


More requirements listed below.


Qualifications

Qualifications must be met by the closing date of this announcement.


GL-9: You qualify for the GL-9 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, performing duties such as:

  • Performing physical searches of detained individuals, their vehicles, and their immediate surroundings for weapons, contraband, currency, and other evidence
  • Apprehending, physically restraining or working with law enforcement officials to identify or apprehend violators of state, federal, or immigration laws
  • Proficient in the use of firearms, preparing investigative reports, serving court orders (e.g., warrants, subpoenas, etc.) and gathering evidence for criminal cases prosecuted through the court system

GS-11: You qualify for the GS-11 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experienceequivalent to at least the next lower grade level, with the authority granted by the state or government to enforce laws, make arrests, and investigate crimes, performing primary duties in an official law enforcement capacity such as:

  • Utilizing intelligence information to track illegal operations, criminal activity, threats to our nation, and/or contraband while serving as a state, Federal, or military law enforcement official
  • Leading investigations of fraud, contraband, criminal activity, threats to our nation, and/or illegal operations to determine sources and patterns while serving as a state, Federal, or military law enforcement official
  • Apprehending violators of state, federal or immigration laws by utilizing various forms of complex technology that includes surveillance, detection, situation awareness systems, and/or communications equipment


The above experience will be applied in connection with the Border Patrol Individual Occupational Requirement: Make arrests and exercise sound judgment in the use of firearms; deal effectively with people in a courteous manner in connection with law enforcement matters; analyze information rapidly and make prompt decisions; or develop and maintain contact with a network of informants.


National Service Experience: refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.


Experience as a CBP Explorer may be qualifying if your resume provides sufficient information to credit your experience. To receive full credit for your experience, please be sure to describe your duties, roles and responsibilities in detail.


Background Investigation: This position is a sensitive National Security position and, upon selection, applicants will be required to undergo, and must successfully pass, a Tier 5 investigation or equivalent for placement and retention.


Language Proficiency: Border Patrol work requires the ability to speak and read Spanish, as well as English. Agents will be provided training to become proficient with the Spanish language at the academy.



Uniform/Grooming Standards: This position requires wearing an officially approved uniform and complying with established grooming standards; as established by the Border Patrol's Uniform and Grooming Standards Policy #IOP-5320-02A-UGSBPA. Updated guidance: Please note that in accordance with these standards, tattoos and/or brandings on the head or face are not permitted. Obscene, derogatory and/or gang tattoos or brandings shall not be visible.


Education

There is no education substitution for these grade levels.


Medical Requirements: Following a tentative job offer, candidates must undergo and successfully complete a medical screening process. Individuals must be medically and physically capable of performing the essential job functions and duties of the position safely and efficiently without endangering the health and safety of the individual, others, or national security.


Drug Testing Requirements: Employees are subject to drug testing in compliance with the DHS Drug-Free Workplace Program. You must complete a drug test as a condition of employment.


Physical Fitness Test: You will be required to successfully pass the Fitness Test.


Interview Process: You will be required to pass a structured interview.


Rigorous Law Enforcement Officer Special Retirement Coverage: This is a rigorous position subject to mandatory retirement under the special retirement provisions for law enforcement officers under CSRS and FERS (5 CFR 842.803 and 5 CFR 831.903, Conditions for Coverage; 5 USC 8425(b) and 5 USC 8335(b), Mandatory Separation; and 5 USC 8412(d) and 5 USC 8336(c), Immediate Retirement). For more information on required years of service and retirement age, click on this link. For further information on when an employee continues or discontinues coverage under the special retirement system for law enforcement officers, please see the CSRS and FERS handbook, Chapter 46 (CSRS pages 12-14, and FERS pages 41-43). If you have questions regarding your retirement coverage provisions, please contact the CBP Retirement Operations Center at (202) 863-6180.



Additional information

You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this position.


Probationary Period: You must serve a one-year probationary period during the first year of your initial permanent federal appointment.


Driver's License: You must possess the ability to operate a Government Owned Vehicle. A valid driver's license is required. Any legal restrictions on a driver's license are not acceptable.



Misdemeanor Crime of Domestic Violence: The BPA position is a weapons-carrying position. Any person who has been convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence cannot lawfully possess a firearm or ammunition. Therefore, if you have been convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence, you are not qualified for this position.


After you successfully complete all the pre-employment steps, you will be at the final offer step.


Residency Requirement: U.S. Customs and Border Protection has a residency requirement that applies to all applicants not currently employed by CBP. Individuals are required to have physically resided in the United States or its protectorates (as declared under international law) for at least three (3) of the last five (5) years, before completing an application for CBP employment. If you do not meet the residency requirement and you have been physically located in a foreign location for more than two (2) of the last five (5) years, you may request an exception to determine if you are eligible for a residency waiver by meeting one or more of the following conditions:

5. Working for the U.S. Government as a federal civilian or as a member of the military

6. A dependent of a federal civilian or member of the military who was working for the U.S. Government

7. Working as a contractor employee, a volunteer, consultant or an intern for the U.S. Government

8. Participation in a study abroad program sponsored by a U.S. affiliated college or university

If selected for a position, you must provide documentation to support a request for an exception to the residency requirement.


Career Transition Assistance Program (CTAP) and Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP): To be considered, you must submit the documentation listed in the Required Documents section. View information about CTAP/ICTAP eligibility on OPM's Career Transition Resources website.


Expand additional information

Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution.


Benefits

How you will be evaluated

You will be evaluated for this job based on how well you meet the qualifications above.

This is a Direct Hire Authority announcement. All applicants who meet the minimum qualification requirements will be reviewed. Veteran's Preference and traditional rating and ranking of applicants do not apply to this vacancy. Veterans and Military Spouses will be considered along with all other candidates.


Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., resume, supporting documents, etc.). Review the Qualifications section of this announcement for more information. If you are found qualified and receive a tentative job offer, you will be required to complete and pass all required pre-employment steps before you can receive a final offer.



Knowledge, Skills, Abilities and Other Characteristics (KSAOs): Candidates who meet the minimum qualification requirements are required to possess certain KSAOs to successfully perform the functions of this position. Candidates will need to demonstrate their ability to perform these KSAOs in their resume. The KSAOs are:

  • Knowledge of Immigration and Nationality Law (e.g., non-immigrant classifications, immigrant classifications, inadmissible noncitizens, removable noncitizens, derivative citizenship, 8 USC)
  • Knowledge of the Use of Force Policy (e.g., firearms, less-lethal devices and techniques, qualification requirements)
  • Knowledge of Criminal Law and Procedure (e.g., statutory authority)
  • Skill in Using Physical Techniques (e.g., self-defense, baton, OC spray, PLS)
  • Skill in Using Firearms (e.g., hand gun, shotgun, M-4)
  • Skills in Basic Operation of a Motor Vehicle (e.g., everyday use of vehicles, parallel parking)



Note: The following document requirements relate to a potential subsequent federal employment application, not to CBP Talent Network registration.

Required Documents

All applicants are required to submit a resume.


Resume: A resume in English is required. It must contain your full legal name, phone number, complete work history, a detailed description of your duties, the dates you performed those duties (MM/DD/YY), as well as your hours worked per week. If you are a current or former Federal employee you must include your grade and step information to receive credit for that work experience.

Note: Your resume must only be two pages or less and uploaded under the document type - Resume. No additional document types will be reviewed as part of your resume. Please see the Border Patrol Agent Resume Aid for specific information and examples.


Are you a current or former federal employee? If you are a current/former federal employee, it is recommended you submit your most recent SF-50 "Notification of Personnel Action" form to support your experience. Please do not submit a Performance Award SF-50.


Are you a veteran? If you claim veterans' preference you will be required to submit proof of eligibility as appropriate to your preference type. For more information, see Veterans Preference.

  • 5-point Preference (TP): Submit DD-214 listing the character of service and either qualifying medal(s) or service period.
  • 10-point Preference (CP or CPS): Submit DD-214 listing the character of service and a VA Disability Award letter dated 1991 or later showing the total percentage of the service-connected disability. Submitting an SF-15 with your application is encouraged.
  • 10-point Preference (XP): You MUST submit a Standard Form 15, DD-214 listing the character of service, and the required documentation stated on the SF-15.
  • Currently Serving: If you are currently serving on active duty, or in the National Guard or Reserves, you can submit a written signed statement from the Armed Forces certifying your dates of service, rank, campaign badge(s) and expeditionary medal(s) (if applicable), expected character of service, type of discharge and anticipated date of separation which must be within 120 days from the closing date of this announcement. Prior to entering on duty, you will be required to provide a final DD-214. Members of the Guard and Reserve can submit the most current copy of their Retirement Points Account System (RPAS) document.


Can you claim an age waiver based on Veterans' Preference or previous Law Enforcement service? If you are over the age of 40, you will need to submit proof you are eligible for an age waiver based on either previous federal law enforcement service or veterans' preference. If you are over the maximum age and do not provide the required documentation for an age waiver, you will not receive consideration under this announcement.

  • If you are claiming an age waiver based on Federal law enforcement service, you MUST submit copies of your SF-50s reflecting the beginning date and end date for all creditable Federal civilian (not military) service under Title 5 U.S.C. 8331(20), and Title 5 U.S.C. 8401(17) showing Retirement Code M or O in Block 30 of your SF-50s.
  • If you are claiming an age waiver based on Veterans' Preference, you must submit the required Veterans' Preference documents.


Are you claiming special priority selection rights under the Career Transition Assistance Program (CTAP) or Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP)? You must submit the separation notice from your agency, your most recent performance rating and your most recent SF-50 with your current position, grade level, and duty location.

job.title: Customs and Border Protection Officer (CBPO) - Evergreen
job.description:
CUSTOMS AND BORDER PROTECTION OFFICER (CBPO) | GRADE LEVELS GS-5, GS-7 and GS-9


You Don’t Just Check Passports. You Guard the Nation.


U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is recruiting for full-time Customs and Border Protection Agents at multiple grade levels. Entry level up to candidates with qualifying general experience, education, public safety, security, military police, or law enforcement experience who may be eligible for consideration at higher grade levels.


As a CBPO, you are the face—and the shield—of the United States at airports, seaports, and land crossings. You’ll use technology, instinct, and training to protect the country from threats while facilitating lawful travel and trade.


This is federal law enforcement at the intersection of precision, pressure, and purpose.


What You’ll Do

  • Screen travelers, cargo, and vehicles.
  • Enforce customs, immigration, and agriculture laws and regulations.
  • Conduct inspections of individuals, documents, goods, and conveyances.
  • Determine whether individuals are admissible to the United States.
  • Detect suspicious behavior, prohibited goods, and potential security threats.
  • Prevent illegal entry, drug smuggling, and other contraband activity.
  • Protect national security while facilitating lawful travel and international trade.


Minimum Requirements

  • U.S. Citizenship: Must be a U.S. citizen.
  • Residency: Must have maintained primary U.S. residency for at least three of the last five years.
  • Age: Generally must be referred for selection before reaching age 40, subject to applicable exceptions.
  • Background Screening: Must successfully complete applicable background investigation, polygraph, medical, and physical fitness requirements.
  • Driver’s License: Must possess a valid driver’s license.


Age Requirement: In accordance with Public Law 100-238, this position is covered under federal law enforcement retirement provisions. Candidates generally must be referred for selection before their 40th birthday under DHS Directive 251-03. Exceptions may apply to qualifying current or former federal civilian law enforcement officers covered by Title 5 U.S.C. 8336(c) or 8412(d), and Veterans' Preference eligible candidates.

Qualifications — GS-5, GS-7 and GS-9


GS-5 — General Experience or Education

Candidates may qualify through one of the following:

  • Three years of general work experience, including one year equivalent to at least GS-4, demonstrating the ability to meet and deal with people and learn and apply a body of facts; OR
  • A bachelor's degree or completion of a four-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university; OR
  • A qualifying combination of general experience and completed college education.


GS-7 — Specialized Experience or Education

Candidates may qualify through one of the following:

  • One year of qualifying specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level, involving activities such as:
  • Inspecting people, documents, or goods for fraud, criminal activity, or illegal operations.
  • Evaluating facts and documentation while applying federal, state, or local laws.
  • Making regulatory or enforcement determinations that may result in arrests, seizures, fines, or penalties.
  • A bachelor's degree with Superior Academic Achievement (SAA), including qualifying class standing, GPA, or honor society membership; OR
  • One year of graduate-level education; OR
  • A qualifying combination of specialized experience and graduate education.


GS-9 — Advanced Specialized Experience or Education

Candidates may qualify through one of the following:

  • One year of qualifying specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level, involving activities such as:
  • Detaining or arresting suspected violators using appropriate law enforcement procedures.
  • Enforcing laws governing imports, exports, or international shipping.
  • Using intelligence techniques and behavioral analysis to identify potential threats.
  • Conducting law enforcement interviews and determining appropriate actions.
  • A master's degree or higher, two years of progressively higher-level graduate education, or a qualifying LL.B. or J.D.; OR
  • A qualifying combination of specialized experience and graduate education beyond the first 18 semester hours.


GS-9 candidates must also demonstrate applicable knowledge, skills, abilities, and characteristics relating to law enforcement procedures, CBP regulations, inspections, interviewing, decision-making, and detecting smuggling or fraud.


Compensation & Benefits

  • Entry Grade Levels: GS-5, GS-7, or GS-9, depending on qualifications.
  • Annual Base Salary: $41,863–$127,464, depending on grade.
  • Promotion Potential: GS-11 and GS-12.
  • Overtime: Fully trained CBP Officers may be eligible for up to $45,000 in additional annual overtime pay.
  • Recruitment Incentives: Up to $15,000 annually for qualifying priority duty locations, subject to a three- or four-year service agreement.
  • Competitive federal salary progression.
  • Federal health, dental, and other insurance benefits.
  • Paid annual and sick leave.
  • Federal retirement benefits and Thrift Savings Plan participation.
  • Paid federal law enforcement training.


Recruitment incentives are location-dependent and subject to CBP eligibility requirements, final duty assignment, and service agreements.X


Priority Duty Locations: Before you submit your application you will be asked to select your preferred location. The location you select does not affect your application and it does not affect the locations that are offered to you at the time of your final offer. You will be asked to select from one of the following:

  • Arizona: Douglas, Lukeville, Nogales, San Luis
  • California: Andrade, Calexico, Otay Mesa, San Francisco, San Ysidro, Tecate
  • Hawaii: Honolulu
  • Maine: Calais, Eastport, Houlton, Jackman, Madawaska, Van Buren, Vanceboro
  • Minnesota: Grand Portage, International Falls
  • Montana: Raymond, Roosville, Sweetgrass, Wild Horse
  • New Mexico: Columbus
  • New York: Alexandria Bay, Champlain, Massena
  • North Dakota: Dunseith, Maida, Pembina, Portal
  • Texas: Eagle Pass, Presidio
  • Vermont: Beecher Falls, Derby Line, Highgate Springs, Norton, Richford
  • Washington: Blaine, Oroville


NOTE: The above preference locations are expected to have vacancies available in the future, however, if the duty locations do not have vacancies at the time of your final offer, you may be offered a different duty location within the United States.


**Recruitment Incentive** Newly appointed Customs and Border Protection Officers who select a prioritized location at the time of their final offer will be offered up to a $15,000 incentive per year with a three-year service contract. Prioritized locations include: Arizona: Douglas, Lukeville, Nogales, San Luis; California: Calexico; Hawaii: Honolulu; Maine: Eastport; Montana: Raymond, Roosville; New Mexico: Columbus; New York: Alexandria Bay, Champlain, Massena, Trout River; North Dakota: Dunseith, Portal; Texas: Eagle Pass; Washington: Blaine


**Recruitment Incentive** Newly appointed Customs and Border Protection Officers who select a prioritized location at the time of their final offer will be offered up to a $15,000 incentive per year with a four-year service contract. Prioritized locations include: California: Otay Mesa, San Francisco, San Ysidro, Tecate; Florida: Key West; Maine: Calais, Houlton, Jackman, Madawaska, Van Buren, Vanceboro; Minnesota: Grand Portage, International Falls; Montana: Sweetgrass; North Dakota: Pembina; Texas: Presidio; Vermont: Beecher Falls, Derby Line, Highgate Springs, Norton, Richford; Washington: Oroville


Duty locations are subject to change. If a preferred location is unavailable when a final offer is made, CBP may offer another location based on operational and mission requirements.

Training


You’ll attend the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC) in Glynco, Georgia, where you will complete approximately 103 days of intensive instruction covering law enforcement procedures, immigration laws, and other essential CBPO skills.


Successful completion of the academy is required. Candidates assigned to certain duty locations may also be required to complete Spanish-language training.


This is not for everyone. But if you’re still reading, maybe it’s for you.

job.title: Senior Rates Analyst - AR
job.description:
Senior Rates Analyst

Department: Pricing & Analytics

Salary Range: $75,000–$80,000 per year

Schedule: Monday–Friday, Day Shift

Position Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented Senior Rates Analyst to support business growth and profitability through pricing strategy, data analysis, and reporting. In this role, you will collaborate closely with analysts and executive sales leadership to evaluate market trends, develop pricing recommendations, and support new and existing business opportunities.

The ideal candidate has strong analytical skills, advanced Microsoft Excel expertise, and the ability to interpret complex data and communicate meaningful business insights while managing multiple priorities and deadlines.

Key Responsibilities

  • Analyze market pricing, historical trends, cost structures, growth objectives, and profitability targets to develop effective pricing strategies.
  • Prepare pricing proposals and bid submissions within tight customer deadlines.
  • Develop and maintain complex Excel formulas, queries, and analytical reports.
  • Research pricing discrepancies, investigate issues, and communicate findings.
  • Track proposals through multiple rounds of pricing revisions and updates.
  • Maintain accurate databases and records for new and revised contract rates, including spot and fixed-term pricing.
  • Manage daily pricing activities, resolve exceptions, and troubleshoot pricing-related issues.
  • Prepare recurring and ad hoc reports for major accounts, identify trends, and summarize findings to support strategic business decisions.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited four-year university, preferably in a quantitative or analytical field.
  • At least 5 years of analyst experience, with 6 or more years of overall professional experience preferred.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including complex formulas, data analysis, and reporting.
  • Strong critical-thinking, problem-solving, and research skills.
  • Experience interpreting data, summarizing results, and presenting actionable insights.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with a structured approach to documentation.
  • Ability to remain composed and productive under pressure while managing changing priorities and tight deadlines.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including comfort working directly with executive leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with KPI reporting and performance metrics.
  • Familiarity with Power BI, Tableau, or other data warehousing and business intelligence tools.
  • A strong interest in numbers, pricing strategy, and business performance.
  • A process-oriented mindset with a focus on accuracy and continuous improvement.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Annual salary of $75,000–$80,000, based on qualifications and experience.
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
  • Supplemental and life insurance options.
  • 401(k) retirement plan with quarterly matching.

Important Application Requirement

Candidates must complete an Excel-based assessment to be considered for this position. Only candidates who complete the assessment will be contacted.

Complete the assessment here:

https://www.ondemandassessment.com/o/JB-65WDU2I62/landing?u=1092983

job.title: Talent Director
job.description:
Talent Director – North America

Location: 100% Remote – U.S.

Compensation: Up to $160,000 annually

Travel: Approximately 10–15%

Reports to: North America HR Vice President


Build the Talent Strategy. Develop the Leaders. Shape the Future.

Our client is seeking an accomplished Talent Director to build and lead an integrated talent strategy across its North American organization.


This is an opportunity for a highly analytical, intellectually curious HR leader who understands the business and can translate organizational needs into practical talent solutions. You’ll have broad responsibility across talent acquisition, learning and development, performance management, leadership development, succession planning, and early-career talent.

This is a highly visible role for a strategic, hands-on leader who enjoys building programs and processes, not simply maintaining them.


What You’ll Lead

  • Develop and execute a comprehensive North American talent strategy and annual roadmap.
  • Provide strategic leadership for talent acquisition, including recruiting strategy, processes, workforce planning, candidate experience, and metrics.
  • Build scalable learning and development programs for employees, managers, and leaders.
  • Design and lead a consistent performance-management and annual review process, including manager training, tools, communications, and governance.
  • Develop leadership-development programs across multiple levels of the organization.
  • Establish succession planning and talent-review processes to identify high-potential talent, assess bench strength, and strengthen the leadership pipeline.
  • Design and lead a structured internship and early-career talent program.
  • Partner with senior leaders and HR Business Partners to translate business priorities into effective talent strategies.
  • Establish meaningful talent metrics and use data to evaluate effectiveness and guide decisions.


What We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate combines intellectual horsepower, business acumen, and practical execution. You can quickly understand complex challenges, develop thoughtful solutions, influence senior leaders, and personally drive initiatives from concept through implementation.


Key qualifications include:

  • 10+ years of progressive Human Resources and/or Talent Management experience
  • 5+ years of HR Business Partner experience, ideally supporting business or operational leadership
  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Organizational Development, or a related field
  • Demonstrated experience in talent acquisition and recruiting
  • Strong experience with learning and development and leadership development
  • Demonstrated success designing and implementing performance-management and performance-review processes
  • Experience building succession-planning and talent-review programs
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, project-management, and communication skills
  • Ability to influence and partner effectively with senior leadership


Experience building or transforming a talent function within a geographically dispersed, multi-site, technical, industrial, engineering, or professional-services organization is highly valued. An advanced degree is a plus.


Who Will Thrive Here

You’re a builder who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. You’re intellectually curious, analytical, pragmatic, and comfortable challenging assumptions. You know how to create structure without unnecessary bureaucracy and understand how talent decisions ultimately affect business performance.

If you’ve built expertise across recruiting, development, performance, and succession—and you’re ready to bring those disciplines together into an integrated talent strategy—this is an opportunity to make a significant and lasting impact.

Compensation: Up to $160,000 annually, based on qualifications and experience.


This search is being conducted confidentially by RCI on behalf of its client. Additional information about the organization will be shared with qualified candidates during the recruitment process.

job.title: Assistant Store Manager
job.description:
Assistant Store Manager – Computer Services


📍 Chicago, IL 60647

💰 $60,000 – $80,000 per year + Bonus


Are you an experienced retail leader with a passion for technology, computers, and customer service?

A leading national technology and consumer electronics retailer is looking for an Assistant Store Manager – Computer Services to lead a busy computer service and repair department.

In this role, you will lead a team of technical professionals, drive customer satisfaction and department performance, and help ensure customers receive exceptional service and technical support.


What You’ll Do

  • Lead the daily operations of the computer service and repair department.
  • Drive customer satisfaction, sales, productivity, and operational performance.
  • Coach, train, and develop a high-performing team.
  • Recruit, hire, onboard, and schedule employees.
  • Ensure customer computer and technical issues are resolved quickly and professionally.
  • Manage department expenses, payroll, and operational goals.
  • Maintain inventory, safety, and operational standards.
  • Support freight flow, merchandising, and store operations.
  • Monitor team training and technical certifications.
  • Serve as Manager-in-Charge when needed.
  • Partner with store leadership to achieve sales, service, and customer experience goals.
